unique_world.visual_theme: A still palm grove with a small stream, a prayer niche and a pavilion facing the sunrise

primary_mechanic.text: A quiet world played by pointing only: each question is answered by pointing at something in the grove, never by choosing words, recalling the vow of silence and the pointing in 19:26-29.

unique_world.narrative_structure: Four questions answered by pointing, then the lantern by the bench
environment_behaviour: palm fronds sway; everything that can be pointed at glows softly while a question is open
unique_world.learning_objective: Learn the quiet prayers and mercy of Surah Maryam; answer by looking and noticing

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Garden of Miracles
story_library.children_narration: Prophet Zakariyya prayed to Allah for a child, even though he and his wife were old. Allah answered his prayer and gave him the joyful news of Yahya. Maryam was also given extraordinary news: she would have a son named Isa, by Allah's command. When Maryam was alone and distressed, Allah provided comfort and help for her. The Quran describes a palm tree and water as part of her story. Surah Maryam also remembers Ibrahim and other prophets who were devoted to Allah. These stories teach us that Allah hears prayers, knows our needs, and has power over all things.

world_idea.title: The Sanctuary of Hope
world_idea.description: Explore a prayer sanctuary, a quiet palm grove, and several connected story areas. Activities focus on discovering the narration, observing nature, and learning about hope and devotion.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: Zakariyya, Maryam, Isa, Yahya and Ibrahim are never shown. The palm and stream (19:23-26) are a quiet place; Maryam is not pictured in it.
